claim: A single S3 object can be up to 50 TB in size. Until December 2, 2025 the maximum was 5 TB.
question: What is the maximum size of a single S3 object?

evidence.quote: You store these objects in one or more buckets, and each object can be up to 50 TB in size.

| [Large object support](#WhatsNew) | Amazon S3 has increased the maximum size of an object you can store in an S3 bucket from 5 TB to 50 TB. For uploading these larger objects, you must implement the Multipart Upload REST API to upload objects in parts, and when downloading these objects, use concurrent `GetObject` requests, as single GET requests are limited to 5 TB. For more information, see [Uploading objects](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/upload-objects.html) and [Downloading objects](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/download-objects.html). | December 2, 2025 |

note: Raised from 5 TB on December 2, 2025; older exam material assumes 5 TB. Single GET requests are still limited to 5 TB per the same row.

claim: A single PUT operation can upload one object of up to 5 GB; larger objects need multipart upload.
question: What is the largest object that one PUT request can upload?

qualifiers.condition: single operation through the SDKs, REST API or AWS CLI

evidence.quote: **Upload an object in a single operation by using the AWS SDKs, REST API, or AWS CLI** – With a single `PUT` operation, you can upload a single object up to 5 GB in size.
**Upload an object in parts by using the AWS SDKs, REST API, or AWS CLI**** –** Using the multipart upload API operation, you can upload a single large object, up to 50 TB in size.

claim: Restore requests from the S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval, S3 Glacier Deep Archive and S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage classes are limited to 1,000 transactions per second per account; above that rate requests are throttled with a ThrottlingException, and S3 Batch Operations can restore many objects in one request.
question: How many restore requests per second does an account get for archived objects?

qualifiers.condition: RestoreObject requests for S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval, S3 Glacier Deep Archive or S3 Intelligent-Tiering objects

evidence.quote: S3 Glacier supports restore requests at a rate of 1,000 transactions per second. If this rate is exceeded otherwise valid requests are throttled or rejected and Amazon S3 returns a `ThrottlingException` error. You can use S3 Batch Operations to retrieve many objects with a single request, which fully utilizes the restore request rate available in your account.

claim: S3 Glacier restores large datasets at up to 1–2 petabytes per day per customer account; any object larger than 5 terabytes restores at up to 300 megabytes per second, so a 50-terabyte S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval object could take up to 48 hours.
question: How fast can an account restore a very large archive, and why does a huge single object take longer?

values.spoken: one to two petabytes per day

qualifiers.condition: contact AWS Support for higher restoration limits

evidence.quote: After you initiate restore requests, S3 Glacier supports restoring large datasets at a throughput of up to 1–2 petabytes per day per customer account. For any retrieval option, objects larger than 5 terabytes will take longer to be restored with up to 300 megabytes per second of retrieval throughput. For example, a 50-terabyte S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval object could take up to 48 hours to complete. If you require increased restoration limits, you can contact AWS Support.

claim: One unit of provisioned capacity guarantees at least 3 Expedited retrievals every 5 minutes from S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and up to 300 megabytes per second of retrieval throughput; without it, Expedited retrievals might not be accepted during periods of high demand.
question: What does one unit of S3 Glacier provisioned capacity give you, and what happens without it?

values.spoken: three expedited retrievals every five minutes

qualifiers.condition: Expedited retrievals from S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval

evidence.quote: Each unit of capacity provides that at least three Expedited retrievals can be performed every 5 minutes, and it provides up to 300 megabytes per second of retrieval throughput.

Without provisioned capacity, Expedited retrievals might not be accepted during periods of high demand. For predictable, fast access to more of your data, consider using the [S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval](https://aws.amazon.com/s3/storage-classes/glacier/instant-retrieval/) storage class.

claim: The default general purpose bucket quota of 10,000 per account was raised from 100 in November 2024, and any customer can request a quota increase up to 1 million buckets.
question: How far can the general purpose bucket quota be raised above the default?

evidence.quote: By default, you can create up to 10,000 general purpose buckets per AWS account. To request a quota increase for general purpose buckets, visit the [Service Quotas console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/servicequotas/home/services/s3/quotas/).
Amazon S3 has increased the default bucket quota from 100 to 10,000 per AWS account. Additionally, any customer can request a quota increase up to 1 million buckets.
